title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I will just write a few lines to let thee know how we are and that I should be glad if thee could come and Bring little James with thee and what other company suits. Our pears is just a beginning to be ripe and I want thee to have some and I may inform that I received a few lines from thee that gave an account of our not receiving all our flax & also one that gave an account of Abraham Warrington’s flax I had an opportunity to send a few lines as far as Henry Warrington’s the next day & I expect to get ours tomorrow, now I may inform thee that we are all in reasonable health which I esteem as a great favor and should be glad to hear from thee and thine if thee cannot come for I think I cannot come on at least it will not suit until this busy time is a little over.

closer.salute: So I conclude with love to thee and thine which my husband joins me in please to give our love to all the family,
